title: Count Permutations Producing the Same BST
statement:
You are given the **preorder traversal** of a binary search tree whose `n` values are all distinct. A BST is built from a sequence of values by inserting them one by one into an initially empty tree: each new value walks down from the root, going left if it is smaller than the current node and right if it is larger, and becomes a new leaf where the walk ends.

The given preorder is one insertion order that produces the tree (inserting the values in preorder reproduces the same BST). Count how many **other** permutations of the same `n` values, used as insertion orders, produce exactly the same BST (same shape and same values). The given order itself is not counted.

The answer can be large, so print it modulo `1000000007`.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer finished the round with the classic puzzle of 3 bulbs and 3 switches (find which switch controls which bulb). This is not tested here.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` distinct integers: the preorder traversal of the BST.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the number of other insertion orders that give the same BST, modulo 1000000007.
constraints: The input is a valid BST preorder; the tree depth is at most n ≤ 3000

examples.explanation: Root 2 must be inserted first. Then 1 and 3 can come in either order, giving 2 orders in total. One of them is the given one, so 1 other order remains.

Root 4 is inserted first. The left subtree {1, 3, 2} is a forced chain, so it has 1 valid order. In the right subtree {5, 7, 6, 8, 11, 10}, the root 5 has only a right child; below it, 7 has the single left value 6 and the forced chain 8, 11, 10 on the right, so 6 can be placed in any of 4 positions relative to that chain: 4 valid orders. The 3 left values interleave with the 6 right values in C(9, 3) = 84 ways, giving 84 * 1 * 4 = 336 orders in total. Excluding the given one leaves 335.
The tree is a chain; every value must be inserted after its parent, which forces the order 1, 2, 3, 4. Only the given order works, so 0 others.

hints: The first element of the preorder is the root, and it must be inserted first in any valid order. The remaining elements split into those smaller than the root (left subtree) and those larger (right subtree), contiguous in the preorder.

Only the relative order inside each subtree matters for that subtree's shape. The two subtrees can be interleaved in any way, so count the interleavings with a binomial coefficient and multiply by the number of valid orders of each subtree.

If `ways(T) = C(|L| + |R|, |L|) * ways(L) * ways(R)` counts all valid orders of a tree, the answer is `ways(root) - 1`. Precompute factorials and inverse factorials modulo 1000000007 so each binomial is O(1), and use an explicit stack if you want to avoid deep recursion.
